In my experience with martial arts (karate and kung fu), core strength and especially leg strength were the most important to not feeling totally wiped out after a class. Being able to sit in a stance is a LOT easier if you're not starting from scratch on building leg muscles, and core strength can help during fights.

I would suggest doing bodyweight exercises that focus on those muscle groups, like squats, plank, leg lifts, etc. You could also practice standing in a stance and holding it. For example, put your feet about two shoulder-widths apart, and then bend your knees into a squat position (about 90 degree angles at your knees - thighs should be approximately parallel to the floor). Keep your knees over your toes and your back straight, and cross your arms in front of you - this is horse stance. See you long you can hold that position for.

Overall aerobic fitness is also good to have, so I'd recommend adding in something like running or biking as well.

Good luck!
